purpose: Measure a zero-gradient temperature-plus-split-CP peripheral recalibration API on frozen new non-PID artifacts. This descriptive diagnostic never selects an operating model, sample count or policy.
selection: First n objects in the existing temperature split and first n in the independent conformal split. Total labels=2*n. Reuse only already charged primary teacher records, no additional objective/filter calls. Primary study calibration at 128/256 is not changed.
inference: Fixed CPU float64, single object (1,16) mapping; frozen model hashes before and after. Fit only temperatures then independent CP quantiles, alpha=.10, complete sets and monitor mode.
diagnostics: For all nine fixed model/sample-count combinations, report per-axis teacher-label inclusion and complete-set size on the same independent 256 initial-state test objects. No test-driven choice, refitting, hard Hold, risk head or acceptance change. Correlated descriptive comparisons, no multiplicity-adjusted statistical or universal guarantee.
interpretation: A measured millisecond CPU fit is only peripheral compute after logits and valid labels exist. It is not millisecond end-to-end personalization, evidence that tens of labels yield useful compact sets, a cross-day/domain-shift guarantee, or clinical/hardware validation. Fresh target-domain labels, a fixed inference mapping and exchangeability premises remain caller responsibilities. Parameter holding and retrospective rollback do not establish physical safety.
